fix_commit.message: Fix potential infinite loop of RANDOMKEY during client pause (#13863)
fix_commit.author: Benson-li

findings.title: dbRandomKey() loop-break guard ignores client-pause expire suppression, causing infinite loop
findings.message: dbRandomKey() retries dictGetFairRandomKey() in a while(1) loop whenever the randomly-picked key is volatile and logically expired, relying on expireIfNeeded() to either actually delete the key (allowing the loop to terminate on a non-expired pick) or on a maxtries safety valve to force termination when the DB cannot make progress. The safety valve `if (allvolatile && server.masterhost && --maxtries == 0) return keyobj;` was written in 2018 to cover only the replica case, where expireIfNeeded() always returns 1 (treats the key as expired) without deleting it, because replicas never delete expired keys themselves. This same commit (47579bdf5, 'Add support for client pause WRITE (#8170)') introduced a second scenario in which expireIfNeeded() also returns 1 without deleting the key: when the server is paused via CLIENT PAUSE (checkClientPauseTimeoutAndReturnIfPaused() in expireIfNeeded, src/db.c ~line 1523-1527). On a primary/master instance (server.masterhost == NULL) whose keyspace consists entirely of volatile keys that are all already logically expired, and which is currently under a client pause, dbRandomKey() will repeatedly: pick a key -> find it has an expire set -> skip the masterhost-gated safety check (since server.masterhost is NULL) -> call expireIfNeeded() which returns 1 without deleting the key because the server is paused -> continue the loop and try again. Because the dictionary never shrinks and the random key is always the same logically-expired volatile key (or one of a small set), the function never returns and the event loop hangs, causing a denial of service. The maxtries safeguard added here needed to also break out of the loop when pause-driven expire suppression (not just replica-driven expire suppression) is in effect, but it was never updated to do so when client-pause write support was introduced.
findings.suggestion: Make the dbRandomKey() loop-termination guard aware of every condition under which expireIfNeeded() can refuse to delete an expired key, not only server.masterhost. Specifically, OR in the client-pause/expire-suppressed condition (later expressed as isPausedActions(PAUSE_ACTION_EXPIRE)) so the maxtries safety valve also fires when the server is a primary that is currently pause-suppressing expirations.

ground_truth.root_cause: An exit-condition invariant in dbRandomKey() ('the only way expireIfNeeded() can refuse to delete an expired key without eventually returning 0 is if this is a replica') was silently broken when a second such path (client-pause-driven expire suppression on a primary) was introduced elsewhere, without the dbRandomKey() guard being updated to match the new invariant.
